result.title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
result.summary: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed to assess emerging hypotheses. Their spatial attention guides view placement, contextual responses determine crop extent, and observation history encourages complementary inspection. The resulting predictions are combined through uncertainty-weighted voting. On ScreenSpot-Pro, SPARK improves grounding accuracy over single-view inference by 13.9, 25.2, and 16.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and UI-TARS, outperforming all compared test-time methods for each backbone. Consistent gains across four additional benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse interfaces and grounding tasks. These results establish semantic probing as an effective mechanism for turning a frozen VLM's understanding of what to inspect into more accurate GUI grounding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的 SPARK 框架，让冻结 VLM 通过「探索探针」描述上下文与关键细节、「验证探针」指出评估假设所需证据，再用其空间注意力与上下文响应决定裁剪位置和范围，并以不确定性加权投票融合多次观测，提升 GUI grounding 精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及「看哪里」的视觉证据筛选与测试时计算分配，与 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本、证据互补与停止决策相关；可核查其探针注意力如何定位裁剪区、观测历史如何避免重复并隐含终止条件，以及投票机制对多视图证据的加权合理性。
